issues.title: Slack notifications not functioning - event listeners never registered
issues.description: The slack.listen() call was removed from the service initialization in Promise.all, but the slack service module is still imported. This means the Slack service event listeners for 'post.published' and 'slack.test' events are never registered during boot. As a result, posts published on the site will not trigger Slack webhook notifications even when Slack integration is configured correctly. The slack.listen() method registers critical event handlers that connect the Ghost event system to the Slack notification service, and without this call, the integration is completely non-functional.

issues.title: Post scheduling will fail on boot - missing required apiUrl parameter
issues.description: The scheduling.init() call is missing the required apiUrl parameter that was previously passed via urlUtils.urlFor('api', {type: 'admin'}, true). The PostScheduler constructor explicitly checks for this parameter and throws an IncorrectUsageError if it's not provided. This will cause Ghost to crash during the boot sequence when attempting to initialize the scheduling service. The apiUrl is critical for the scheduling service as it's used to generate signed admin tokens and callback URLs for scheduled post publishing. Without this parameter, the scheduled publishing feature cannot function.

issues.title: Race condition in email service initialization - dependency order violated
issues.description: The emailAddressService.init() was moved from sequential await execution into the parallel Promise.all block alongside emailService.init(). The comment explicitly states 'newsletter service and email service depend on email address service', indicating a required initialization order. The EmailServiceWrapper's init() method imports and uses emailAddressService, expecting it to be fully initialized. By running these initializations in parallel, emailService may attempt to access emailAddressService before it has completed initialization, leading to undefined behavior, null reference errors, or incorrect email configuration. This race condition can cause intermittent failures that are difficult to reproduce and debug.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25799 - Removed xmlrpc/pingomatic ping service

structured_output.summary:
The PR deletes the legacy XML-RPC/Pingomatic ping service (`server/services/xmlrpc.js` and its unit test), removes its `xmlrpc.listen()` call from `boot.js`, and drops the `privacy.useRpcPing` flag from the development config. The xmlrpc removal itself is clean: nothing else in core or tests references `xmlrpc`, `useRpcPing`, or `pingomatic` after the change, and the `xml` package is still needed by the sitemap generators, so it stays.

The `boot.js` hunk, however, goes well beyond the xmlrpc removal and the PR description does not mention it. It also deletes `slack.listen()`, which silently disables Slack post-published notifications and the Slack test endpoint, and it changes `scheduling.init({apiUrl})` to `scheduling.init()`. The scheduler throws when `apiUrl` is missing, so the second change is a boot-time crash. Those two changes must be reverted or justified before this merges.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The scheduler change will make Ghost fail to boot: `scheduling.init()` is called without options, and `post-scheduling/index.js` reads `options.apiUrl` inside an async function, so `initServices()` rejects. The Slack listener removal silently breaks Slack notifications, and neither change is described in the PR. The xmlrpc deletion itself is correct.

architecture.overview:
Ghost boots through `initServices()` in `ghost/core/core/boot.js`. That function awaits `stripe.init()` and then `emailAddressService.init()`, and runs the remaining services concurrently in one `Promise.all`. Several services register listeners on the shared `events` bus (`post.published`, `slack.test`), and `scheduling.init` needs the Admin API URL to schedule posts. Before this PR, the Pingomatic ping was one of those listeners, registered through `xmlrpc.listen()`.

The PR removes the xmlrpc service and its boot-time listener, along with its config flag. Because the same hunk edits the `Promise.all` list, it also removes `slack.listen()` and changes the scheduler's init call. Those two edits affect services that are unrelated to xmlrpc.
steps: Entry point: `initServices()` in `ghost/core/core/boot.js` runs `stripe.init()`, then `emailAddressService.init()`, then a `Promise.all` over the remaining services.
Removed: `xmlrpc.listen()` and the `xmlrpc` require. The service is deleted from `server/services/xmlrpc.js`, which previously subscribed to `post.published` on the shared events bus.

Unintended removal: `slack.listen()` is gone from the `Promise.all`. In `server/services/slack.js`, `listen()` registers the `post.published` Slack webhook and the `slack.test` handler, so both stop firing.

Changed: `scheduling.init({apiUrl: urlFor('api', ...)})` became `scheduling.init()`. `server/adapters/scheduling/post-scheduling/index.js` reads `options.apiUrl`, so the call throws when no options are passed.

Moved: `emailAddressService.init()` moved from a standalone `await` into the `Promise.all`. `EmailAddressServiceWrapper.init()` is synchronous, so the ordering holds in practice, but the NOTE comment above it is now detached from the code it describes.
Config: `privacy.useRpcPing` is removed from `config.development.json`. No other reference remains.

findings.title: Boot crashes because scheduling.init() is called without apiUrl
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js`, the `scheduling.init()` call inside the `Promise.all` in `initServices()` (around line 368) was changed to take no arguments. `server/adapters/scheduling/post-scheduling/index.js` requires `options.apiUrl`, so boot fails. Restore the original argument `{apiUrl: urlUtils.urlFor('api', {type: 'admin'}, true)}`. The `urlUtils` require at line 343 is still needed for this. This change is unrelated to removing xmlrpc, so revert it rather than working around it.

findings.title: slack.listen() removed, silently disabling Slack post notifications
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js`, `slack.listen()` was removed from the `Promise.all` in `initServices()` (around line 351-362). That silently stops Slack `post.published` notifications and the `slack.test` handler, which are both registered by `server/services/slack.js` `listen()`. Restore `slack.listen(),` in the `Promise.all`, in its original position after `permissions.init()`. If the Slack removal was intentional, instead remove the `slack` require and the related service code, and call that out in the PR description.

findings.title: PR diff contains changes not described in the PR
findings.body:
The description covers only xmlrpc/Pingomatic removal. The diff also changes Slack listener registration, the scheduler init options, and the email-address init ordering, and it adds an unrelated NOTE comment about `npm install`. Reviewers reading the description will not expect boot behaviour changes, which is how the scheduler and Slack regressions can get through. Either split the unrelated changes into their own PRs or update the description to list them.

::diff{file="ghost/core/core/boot.js" lines="313-313"}
findings.fixPrompt: This PR's description says it only removes the xmlrpc/Pingomatic service, but `ghost/core/core/boot.js` also changes the Slack listener, the scheduler init options, and the email-address init ordering, and adds an unrelated `npm install` NOTE comment at line 313. Revert the unrelated changes (see the separate findings on the scheduler and Slack regressions). Keep only the xmlrpc require and `xmlrpc.listen()` removal in this PR, and drop the stray comment.

findings.title: Unused urlUtils and slack bindings left in boot.js
findings.body:
After this change, `const slack` (line 319) is unused because `slack.listen()` is gone. `const urlUtils` (line 343) is also unused because `scheduling.init()` no longer uses it. Lint rules such as `no-unused-vars` will flag both. Once the two regressions above are fixed, `urlUtils` is needed again, but `slack` should only be removed if Slack is actually being dropped.

::diff{file="ghost/core/core/boot.js" lines="319-319"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js`, the `const slack = require('./server/services/slack')` binding (around line 319) is unused once `slack.listen()` is removed. Either restore the `slack.listen()` call or remove the binding. Confirm that `urlUtils` (around line 343) is still used after the `scheduling.init` argument is restored, and that lint passes for the file.

findings.title: emailAddressService.init() moved into Promise.all with a dangling comment
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js`, `emailAddressService.init()` was moved into the `Promise.all` in `initServices()` (around line 349-352), and the NOTE comment above it is now detached from any code. Either restore the explicit `await emailAddressService.init();` before the `Promise.all` (the original ordering), or move the NOTE comment onto the `emailAddressService.init()` entry in the array. Keep the ordering dependency explicit either way.

findings.title: No test exercises the boot change, which is how the regressions slipped through
findings.fixPrompt: Add a test covering `initServices()` in `ghost/core/core/boot.js`. It should verify that `scheduling.init` is called with an options object containing a non-empty `apiUrl`, and that `slack.listen` is invoked during boot. Follow the mocking style in the existing `ghost/core/test/unit/server/services/slack.test.js`. The test should fail against the current PR diff.

findings.title: Clean removal of the xmlrpc service and its config flag
findings.body: The xmlrpc deletion is complete. No remaining references to `xmlrpc`, `useRpcPing`, or `pingomatic` exist in core, test, or config. The `xml` package is still required by the sitemap generators in `core/frontend/services/sitemap/`, so the dependency should stay in `package.json`. The deleted test file was tied to the deleted module and does not need a replacement.
